questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: Future perfect: will have + past participle for an action finished before a future time. Example: By 10 p.m. I'll have done my homework.

wrongReasons.will check: 'By two o'clock' shows the action will be complete before then, so use 'will have checked'.
wrongReasons.check: This is about the future with 'by', so the present simple is wrong.

questions.text: Our flight lands at noon, so by two o'clock we ___ (check) into the hotel.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: Future continuous for an action that will be in progress at a specific future time. Example: At noon tomorrow I'll be sitting an exam.

wrongReasons.will fly: 'At this time tomorrow' needs an action in progress: 'will be flying'.
wrongReasons.fly: The present simple cannot describe an action in progress at a future time.

questions.text: At this time tomorrow, the astronauts ___ (fly) towards the space station.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: After 'once' in a future time clause, use the present simple or present perfect. Example: Once you have paid, you will get a receipt.

wrongReasons.will come: After 'once' do not use 'will'; use the present simple.
wrongReasons.came: This is about the future, so the past simple is wrong.

questions.text: Once the new law ___ (come) into force, smoking in parks will be banned.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'By' + a future time usually takes the future perfect. Example: By 2050, cities will have changed a lot.

wrongReasons.will find: 'By 2040' means before that date, so use the future perfect 'will have found'.
wrongReasons.find: This is a prediction about the future, so the present simple is wrong.

questions.text: By 2040, scientists ___ (find) a cure for many types of cancer, I hope.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: Present continuous for fixed future arrangements. Example: I'm meeting Tom for lunch tomorrow.

wrongReasons.will visit: This is a fixed arrangement, so use the present continuous, not 'will'.
wrongReasons.visit: The present simple is not used for personal future arrangements.

questions.text: I can't come on Saturday because I ___ (visit) my grandparents; we arranged it weeks ago.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: After 'while' in a future time clause, use the present simple, not 'will'. Example: I'll water your plants while you are on holiday.

wrongReasons.will be: After 'while' in a future time clause, do not use 'will'.
wrongReasons.was: This is about the future, so use the present simple 'am'.

questions.text: You can borrow my car while I ___ (be) away.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: In the main clause of a future condition, use 'will' + verb. Example: Unless you hurry, you'll be late.

wrongReasons.miss: The main clause talks about the future, so use 'will miss'.
wrongReasons.would miss: This is a real future situation, so use 'will', not 'would'.

questions.text: Unless we leave now, we ___ (miss) the beginning of the show.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: Future perfect (continuous) for duration up to a future event. Example: By the time he finishes, he will have worked for twelve hours.

wrongReasons.will teach: 'By the time' and 'for forty years' need the future perfect.
wrongReasons.teaches: The present simple does not show duration up to a future moment.

questions.text: By the time she retires, Professor Lee ___ (teach) at this university for forty years.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: We use 'will' / 'won't' for promises. Example: I won't be late again, I promise.

wrongReasons.don't tell: Promises about the future use 'won't', not the present simple.
wrongReasons.am not telling: A promise is a decision at the moment of speaking, so use 'won't tell'.

questions.text: I promise I ___ (not / tell) anyone your secret.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: Future perfect with 'already' for something finished before a future moment. Example: When you call, I'll probably have gone to bed.

wrongReasons.will probably eat: 'Already' shows the meal will be finished before you arrive, so use 'will have eaten'.
wrongReasons.are probably eating: The meal will be finished, not in progress, so use the future perfect.

questions.text: When you arrive, we ___ (probably / eat) already, so have a snack on the way.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: Use 'will' for offers and decisions made at the moment of speaking. Example: It's cold. I'll close the window.

wrongReasons.help: An offer made now about the next moment needs 'will help'.
wrongReasons.am helping: This is a sudden offer, not a planned arrangement, so use 'will'.

questions.text: Hold on, I ___ (help) you carry those heavy bags.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Afford' is followed by 'to' + verb. Example: We can't afford to go on holiday.

wrongReasons.buying: 'Afford' is followed by the infinitive with 'to', not the -ing form.
wrongReasons.buy: You need 'to' before the verb after 'afford'.

questions.text: I can't afford ___ (buy) a new car this year.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind' is followed by the -ing form. Example: Would you mind waiting a moment?

wrongReasons.to open: 'Mind' is followed by the -ing form, not 'to' + verb.

questions.text: Would you mind ___ (open) the window? It's very hot in here.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Manage' is followed by 'to' + verb. Example: He managed to fix the car.

wrongReasons.finish: You need 'to' before the verb after 'managed'.

questions.text: She managed ___ (finish) the marathon despite her injury.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Remember + -ing' is about a memory of a past action; 'remember to' is about a duty. Example: I remember meeting her at a party.

wrongReasons.to lock: 'Remember to do' is about not forgetting a duty; here you have a memory of a past action, so use -ing.
wrongReasons.lock: After 'remember' use the -ing form or 'to' + verb, never the bare verb.

questions.text: I remember ___ (lock) the door, so I'm sure the house is safe.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + -ing' means to quit an activity; 'stop to do' means to stop in order to do something. Example: She stopped eating meat.

wrongReasons.to smoke: 'Stop to smoke' means you stopped another activity in order to smoke, which is the opposite meaning.
wrongReasons.smoke: After 'stop' use the -ing form for the activity you quit.

questions.text: My doctor told me I smoked too much, so I stopped ___ (smoke) last year.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Forget to do' is about a future duty or task. Example: Don't forget to buy bread.

wrongReasons.sending: 'Forget + -ing' is about a past memory; for a task to do, use 'to send'.
wrongReasons.send: You need 'to' before the verb after 'forget'.

questions.text: Don't forget ___ (send) the invoice to the client.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form. Example: I look forward to hearing from you.

wrongReasons.see: Here 'to' is a preposition, so the verb must take -ing.
wrongReasons.seen: After the preposition 'to' use the -ing form, not the past participle.

questions.text: We're really looking forward to ___ (see) you at the wedding.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Make someone do' uses the base form without 'to' in the active. Example: She made me apologise.

wrongReasons.to rewrite: After 'make + person' in the active, use the base form without 'to'.
wrongReasons.rewriting: 'Make someone' is followed by the base form, not the -ing form.

questions.text: The teacher made us ___ (rewrite) the whole essay.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Be used to' means 'be accustomed to' and is followed by the -ing form. Example: I'm used to getting up early.

wrongReasons.work: In 'be used to', 'to' is a preposition, so use the -ing form.
wrongReasons.worked: After 'be used to' the verb takes -ing, not the past form.

questions.text: She is used to ___ (work) night shifts at the hospital.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Agree' is followed by 'to' + verb. Example: He agreed to help us.

wrongReasons.share: You need 'to' before the verb after 'agreed'.

questions.text: They agreed ___ (share) the costs of the repair.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Avoid' is followed by the -ing form. Example: She avoids driving at night.

wrongReasons.answer: After 'avoid' the verb needs the -ing form.

questions.text: He avoided ___ (answer) the journalist's questions.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Regret to tell/inform' is a formal way to give bad news; 'regret + -ing' means being sorry about a past action. Example: We regret to say the flight is cancelled.

wrongReasons.telling: 'Regret telling' means you are sorry you told someone something before; for giving bad news now, use 'regret to tell'.
wrongReasons.tell: After 'regret' use 'to' + verb or the -ing form, never the bare verb.

questions.text: I regret ___ (tell) you that your application has been unsuccessful.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'It's no use' is followed by the -ing form. Example: It's no use crying about it.

wrongReasons.to complain: 'It's no use' is followed by the -ing form, not 'to' + verb.
wrongReasons.complain: After 'It's no use' the verb needs -ing.

questions.text: It's no use ___ (complain); the manager won't change his mind.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Let someone do' uses the base form without 'to'. Example: They let us play in the garden.

wrongReasons.to stay: After 'let + person', use the base form without 'to'.
wrongReasons.staying: 'Let someone' is followed by the base form, not the -ing form.

questions.text: My parents let me ___ (stay) out until midnight.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Consider' is followed by the -ing form. Example: We are considering buying a house.
questions.text: The company is considering ___ (move) its headquarters to Berlin.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Pretend' is followed by 'to' + verb; the negative is 'pretend not to'. Example: He pretended not to see me.

wrongReasons.not hearing: 'Pretend' is followed by 'not to' + verb, not the -ing form.
wrongReasons.didn't hear: After 'pretended' you need an infinitive: 'not to hear'.

questions.text: She pretended ___ (not / hear) what I said.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Would like' is followed by 'to' + verb. Example: I'd like to learn the piano.

wrongReasons.visiting: 'Would like' takes 'to' + verb, not the -ing form.
wrongReasons.visit: You need 'to' before the verb after 'would like'.

questions.text: I'd like ___ (visit) Japan one day.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: After a preposition such as 'of', use the -ing form. Example: She was accused of cheating.

wrongReasons.lie: After the preposition 'of', the verb must take the -ing form.
wrongReasons.lied: After 'of' use the -ing form, not the past simple.

questions.text: He was accused of ___ (lie) to the police.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'Risk' is followed by the -ing form. Example: Don't risk missing your flight.
questions.text: We can't risk ___ (lose) our biggest customer.

questions.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: After the preposition in 'think of/about', use the -ing form. Example: She's thinking about changing jobs.

wrongReasons.take: After the preposition 'of', the verb must take -ing.
wrongReasons.to take: 'Think of' is followed by the -ing form, not 'to' + verb.

questions.text: I'm thinking of ___ (take) a year off to travel.
